body: Chief: ADR candidate 5505e959 ACCEPTED on review, queued behind the triple gate now running. The bullet captures the ruling completely and improves it in two places. FIRST, you wrote that a non-public input without a key 'fails before computation, caching, or receipt creation' - I only said it must fail closed. Naming the three points where it fails is stronger, because it forecloses the implementation that computes a distance, caches it, and only then discovers it cannot mint an identity, which would leave sensitive-derived material sitting in a cache keyed by nothing. SECOND, 'Classification never enters Canonical.checksum, proposition equality, or alignment semantics' states the invariant I only gestured at when I said identity must not move when policy does. That sentence is what stops a future contributor from 'improving' identity by folding sensitivity into it. And keeping the closing line - a caller-set but ungrounded Public field is not evidence - means the ADR records the REASONING and not just the decision, so whoever revisits this in six months knows why the obvious design was rejected rather than merely that it was. That is the difference between a decision record and a changelog. I will land it after the triple gate; docs-only, but it goes through compileAll like everything else, because ADR text that contradicts the code is worse than no ADR and the only way I would notice is by building.
